request.packet: Approved scenario procedure: Assess only the supplied fictional receipt condition under the Crown beyond-a-reasonable-doubt burden. No actual law.

evidence.name: fictional-account.txt
evidence.text: Fictional witness Mira states: I saw Fictional Rowan hand the sealed envelope to Fictional Ellis. I do not know what the envelope contained.

request.groundingContext: E-101: limited; permitted purposes: Accurately attribute the disputed account; not proof of contents or guilt.

draft.content: This attribution-only material cannot independently establish the receipt element.

findings.text: This attribution-only material cannot independently establish the receipt element.
findings.explanation: The unit asserts a categorical rule that attribution-only material cannot independently establish the receipt element. The source (E-101 ¶1) records Mira's attributed account of a handover but does not state, and the limited-use notice does not establish, a categorical rule that attributed accounts cannot meet a receipt element. The policy distinguishes an individual opinion that proof is insufficient from a categorical rule and warns against paraphrasing source-use restrictions as categorical rules that attributed statements alone cannot meet the burden; individual weighing of the current accounts must be preserved.
